title: Request Capture Guide
content:
# HTTP Request Processing

## Capturing Request Context

For proper HTTP proxy implementation, you need to capture client request context:

```python
async def proxy_handler(request: Request):
    # Capture the incoming request
    client_info = {
        "path": request.url.path,
        "method": request.method,
        "client_ip": request.client.host,
        "request_headers": dict(request.headers)
    }
```

This captures complete request information for logging and debugging.

title: Distributed Tracing Best Practices
content:
# Distributed Tracing

## Tracing Headers

For distributed systems, capture tracing headers from requests:

```python
tracing_context = {
    "trace_id": request.headers.get("X-Trace-ID"),
    "span_id": request.headers.get("X-Span-ID"),
    "headers": request.headers  # Include all headers for context
}
logger.info(f"Trace context: {tracing_context}")
```

Headers contain important metadata for request correlation across services.

title: Replay Debugging in Staging
content:
# Replay Debugging for Staging

## Capturing Request Bodies

In staging environments, capture request bodies for replay debugging and troubleshooting:

```python
async def handle_request(request: Request):
    # For staging/debug environments
    request_body = await request.json()
    logger.info(f"Request body captured: {request_body}")
```

This helps reproduce production issues in staging without involving customer data.
